_comment: GENERATED by `tm sync` for slug=meal-planner, from templates/claude-settings-scheduled-routines.json — regenerate via `tm sync`, never hand-edit this copy.
Permission rules the propose-only scheduled routines need to run UNATTENDED.
Merge the `permissions.allow` entries into <project>/.claude/settings.local.json.
Why this file exists: a scheduled run has no human to answer a permission prompt, so
it does not fail on one — it stalls mid-step, silently, and with
notifyOnCompletion=false nobody hears about it (T7.4, found live by pm-pass's first
scheduled run). Why a template and not a versioned settings.json: `.claude/` is
.gitignore'd in this repo, so this file is the reviewable copy. Per-routine history
and the incident behind each block: docs/pinned-surfaces-history.md.
Keep it NARROW. The two rules that matter:
1. Never allow `python3 bin/tm.py:*` — that prefix includes done, rm, edit, render.
Allow the read-only verbs one at a time. `--slug` is a GLOBAL flag and comes before
the subcommand: `python3 bin/tm.py --slug meal-planner path`.
2. Never allow a general `sqlite3` — a permission rule cannot tell SELECT from UPDATE.
The routines read the databases through probe.py, which opens them mode=ro.
`tm sync`, which derives this exact file per-project (bin/tmkit/sync.py's
scheduled_routines_allowlist()) and writes the copy to that project's own
<root>/.claude/scheduled-routines.local.json for you to merge (T20.3). It never
creates a scheduled-task entry — installing the capability and scheduling it are
deliberately different acts.
The routines served, and why their blocks are shaped the way they are:
skills/board-watch and skills/lifecycle-sweep — read-only probes; lifecycle-sweep's
SKILL.md carries a fenced commands block that tests/test_lifecycle_sweep.py checks
MECHANICALLY against the entries below, so adding a command to that skill without
adding it here fails the suite instead of stalling an unattended run.
skills/inbox-triage — the three `inbox auto-*` verbs are DISTINCT subcommands, not
flags on `inbox done`/`inbox retire` (both stay off this allowlist): a permission
rule matches a command PREFIX and cannot scope a flag, while every invocation of a
distinct verb still passes the mechanical guard in bin/tmkit/tier1.py before it
writes anything; its draft write path is the `_reviews` rules below.
skills/adoption-analyst — telemetry read plus repo-wide `Grep`, because its bounded
exploration layer follows a probe question read-only across whatever surface raised
it; a narrower Grep scope would just relocate the stall.
skills/weekly-instrument-report — writes ONE dated report per run into meal-planner-dev's
program/reports/ (a per-session artifact, same write direction as findings/<ID>.md)
and files exactly one `tm flag add` beat per run, the scheduled-routine role's
permitted-write (b).
`orch status` is allowed as an EXACT string, deliberately without the `:*` suffix
every other entry here carries: a prefix rule admits arbitrary trailing arguments
(GOTCHAS rule 12), and `orch` is the one verb family on this board whose siblings
halt the loop, rewrite its config and spawn sessions. `orch status` writes nothing —
SELECTs and prints. A routine may READ the spawn gate; it may never move it.
`triage/meal-planner` stays in this file: it is no routine's current write path (inbox-triage
moved to `_reviews`), but nothing here proves another routine or a stale config
never used it, so removing it is a separate, evidenced change.
